service.name: Service catalog
service.description:
Lists every tool this host serves, with its route, price and purpose. For any agent deciding whether this host has a tool worth calling.

You provide: Nothing. This service takes no parameters.

You receive: a JSON catalog of every route, its price, and what it is for.

service.name: Rail ping
service.description:
Confirms that a paid call to this host settles end to end. For an integrator proving their x402 client can pay this host before wiring anything expensive.

You provide: Nothing. This service takes no parameters.

You receive: a timestamped acknowledgement, after a real settled payment of $0.01.

service.name: Duplicate check
service.description:
Says whether this exact task, endpoint and parameter set was already paid for recently. For an agent about to retry, that does not want to pay twice for one job.

You provide: policyId (string); taskHash (string); endpoint (string); paramsHash (string).

You receive: whether a matching prior intent exists, which one, and how long the match remains in the window.

service.name: Metadata redaction
service.description:
Strips emails, phone numbers, API keys and bearer tokens out of payment metadata and hashes what is left. For an agent that must attach metadata to a payment without publishing what is inside it.

You provide: metadata (object).

You receive: the redacted metadata and a hash of it, with nothing stored.

service.name: Receipt lookup
service.description:
Reports the anchoring state of a receipt this host wrote. For a caller holding a receiptRef who wants to know whether it has reached the chain.

You provide: receiptId (string).

You receive: the receipt's current state, and its anchoring transaction once it has one.

service.name: Receipt status
service.description:
The same receipt state, as a plain GET a browser or a poller can use. For anything polling for an anchor without wanting to POST.

You provide: Nothing. This service takes no parameters.

You receive: the receipt's state and its anchoring transaction once it has one.

service.name: Approval status
service.description:
Reports whether a payment that was escalated to a human has been approved or denied yet. For an agent waiting on a human decision it triggered.

You provide: Nothing. This service takes no parameters.

You receive: the pending, approved or denied state of one escalation.

service.name: Café menu
service.description:
A machine-readable café menu, used to demonstrate governed spending on something ordinary. For an agent being shown what a governed purchase looks like end to end.

You provide: Nothing. This service takes no parameters.

You receive: the items, their prices, and how long a quote holds.

service.name: Café order
service.description:
Buys a demonstration coffee voucher, to show a real payment against a real policy. For anyone evaluating what a governed agent purchase feels like without spending much.

You provide: Any one of: buyerRef.

You receive: an order id and a pickup code. The fulfilment is a demonstration, not a real coffee.

service.name: Product name suggestions
service.description:
Proposes short product names for an idea, filtered against a list of over-used startup stems. For a founder or an agent naming something new.

You provide: idea (string).

You receive: a handful of candidate names, each with the reasoning behind it.

service.name: Name ranking
service.description:
Orders a list of candidate names by length, character set and how easily they are said. For someone choosing between names they already have.

You provide: names (array).

You receive: the names in ranked order with their scores.

service.name: Domain availability
service.description:
Asks the registries whether the domains for a list of names are taken. For someone checking whether a name is usable before committing to it.

You provide: names (array).

You receive: one availability verdict per domain, with the registry response behind it.

service.name: Launch checklist
service.description:
Returns a short launch checklist for a chosen brand name. For someone who has picked a name and is about to launch.

You provide: name (string).

You receive: a list of concrete steps, using the name given.

service.name: Launch brand pack
service.description:
Runs naming, domain checking, ranking and the launch checklist as one call. For a founder or an agent wanting a first pass at a brand in a single request.

You provide: idea (string).

You receive: candidate names, their domain verdicts, a ranking, and a launch checklist.
